findings.F1: The book earns too little because it is rarely in and small when in: it holds a position on 24.4 % of bars at a mean size of 0.55 of the book, so its mean daily return is 0.044 % against the coins' 0.119 %, though it gains 0.19 % per bar while in.
findings.F2: The move after a break outlasts the 5-day holding. The excess return over the coin's drift from the 878 entries is +1.15 % over 5 days (t 3.3, 849 cases), +2.24 % over 10 days (t 4.0, 815), +3.76 % over 20 days (t 3.4, 775) and +8.7 % over 40 days (t 3.8, 631). The increments after day 5 stay positive: days 6–10 +1.45 % (t 3.8), days 11–20 +1.71 % (t 2.6), days 21–40 +5.6 % (t 4.5).
findings.F3: Distance above the 50-day average does not grade the move, yet it sets the size. Across distance quartiles of 1.7 %, 5.3 %, 10.2 % and 22.9 %, the 5-day return is 1.3 %, 1.9 %, 1.9 % and 1.8 %, and the 20-day return is 5.0 %, 9.2 %, 5.9 % and 4.4 %. The verdict's slope is -6.8e-5. The lowest quartile is held at a mean allocation of 0.22 against 0.61 to 0.82 for the others.
findings.F4: Breaks that come after a falling 60-day return do not continue. In the quartile with a mean 60-day return of -10.6 %, the 20-day excess return is -1.7 % (10-day +0.7 %). The three other quartiles give +5.6 % to +14.1 % (top minus bottom t 1.89, about 95 cases each).
findings.F5: The losing breaks are concentrated in falling years. The 20-day excess return is -26 % in 2018 (24 cases), -2.8 % in 2022 (68) and -1.1 % in 2023 (161), against +13.8 % in 2020 (122) and +5.5 % in 2024 (134).
findings.F6: Cost is not the cause. The total 5-day move per case is 1.61 %, against a round-trip cost of 0.19 %, and the 1119 trades average +3.17 % net after a mean of 7.3 days.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 20 days, only while its close is above its 50-day average, and the more times the price had turned down at that level, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would hold resistance breaks for weeks rather than days and size them by how often the level had held, not by how far price sits above its average.
ideas.name: resistance break held longer

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above a price where it turned down several times in the past 90 days, it tends to keep rising over the next 20 days, only while its close is above its 50-day average and its 60-day return is positive, and the more times the price had turned down at that level, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would refuse resistance breaks that come after a falling quarter and hold the others for weeks.
ideas.name: breaks after rising quarter
